extracted.intended_audience: parties and counsel participating in FCC administrative hearing proceedings (Part 1)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evidentiary rules for discovery, depositions, subpoenas, evidence, and written-record hearings under FCC Part 1. Covers how to take/use depositions and interrogatories, produce documents, prepare written pleadings (affirmative/responsive/reply), and when oral testimony is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer to propound written interrogatories in depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the taking of depositions upon written interrogatories, the party who served the original interrogatories shall transmit copies of all interrogatories to the officer designated in the notice, who shall propound them to the witness and record the answers verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The officer who conducts the deposition is responsible for reading the interrogatories to the witness and recording verbatim answers; this ensures fidelity to the served interrogatories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of deposition to witness; changes; signing
rubrics_metrics.description: When the testimony is fully transcribed, the deposition shall be submitted to the witness for examination and read to or by him unless examination and reading are waived by the witness and parties. Any changes in form or substance desired by the witness shall be entered with reasons; the deposition shall then be signed by the witness unless signing is waived or the witness is ill, cannot be found, or refuses to sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If witness refuses or cannot sign, the officer shall sign and state on the record the reason (waiver, illness, absence, refusal) and the deposition may be used unless the presiding officer suppresses it upon motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification, sealing, and filing of depositions by officer
rubrics_metrics.description: The officer shall certify that the witness was duly sworn, that the deposition is a true record of the testimony, and that the officer is not counsel or interested; the officer shall seal the deposition and promptly send the original and two copies of the deposition and exhibits, plus the notice and interrogatories, by certified mail to the Secretary of the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification attests impartiality and truth, and certified-mail delivery to the Secretary (original + two copies) is required for filing the deposition and exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to the substance of interrogatories must be made pre-deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is objection to the substance of any interrogatory or to examination on any matter clearly covered by the notice to take depositions, the objection shall be made in a motion opposing the taking of depositions or in a motion to limit or suppress the interrogatory as provided in §§ 1.315(b) and 1.316(d) and shall not be made at the taking of the deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive objections to interrogatories should be raised by motion before the deposition starts; do not wait to object during the deposition to preserve objection on substantive grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely objection requirement for oral deposition errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors and irregularities occurring at oral examination in manner of taking, form of questions or answers, oath, or conduct are waived unless reasonable objection is made at the taking of the deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an objection is made during the deposition, counsel should attempt to agree on corrective measures; if no agreement, the officer notes the objection and the testimony is taken subject to the objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections at depositions for relevancy, privilege, or oppressive conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Objection may be made at the taking of depositions on relevancy or privilege if the notice doesn't clearly indicate the matter; objection may also be made that the examination unreasonably annoys, embarrasses, or oppresses a deponent or party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When objecting to a line of questioning counsel should attempt to agree on limits; if counsel cannot agree, procedures require statements within 24 hours and prompt presiding officer ruling reduced to writing; rulings are not appealable and depositions continue in accordance with the ruling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures when counsel cannot agree on deposition limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If counsel cannot agree on proper limits of examination, taking of depositions continues on non-objected matters and counsel shall, within 24 hours, jointly or individually provide statements of positions to the presiding officer, with contact numbers, or otherwise confer with the presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer must promptly rule or take other action under § 1.313 and reduce the ruling to writing; the taking of depositions continues per that ruling and the ruling is final (not subject to appeal).

rubrics_metrics.name: No inference from favorable action on notice to take depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: No inference concerning the admissibility of a deposition in evidence shall be drawn because of favorable action on the notice to take depositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favorable procedural rulings on notices do not automatically make the deposition admissible; admissibility is judged under the evidence rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to admissibility of depositions may be made as if witness present
rubrics_metrics.description: Objection may be made to receiving any deposition or part thereof for any reason which would require exclusion if the witness were then present and testifying, except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections that could have been obviated if made during the taking of depositions may be deemed waived (see waiver rules for competency, relevancy, privilege).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of objections by failure to object during depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections to competency of a witness, or competency, relevancy, or materiality of testimony, are waived by failure to make them before or during the taking of depositions if the ground could have been obviated or removed at that time; privilege objections are likewise waived if not made before or during the taking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely assertion of competency/relevancy/privilege during deposition is critical to preserve those objections for hearing admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses of depositions at hearing (contradict, impeachment, any lawful purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the hearing, any part or all of a deposition, so far as admissible, may be used against any party who was present or represented at the taking or had due notice, including for contradicting/impeaching, use of party/officer depositions by adverse party for any purpose, and use of any witness deposition for any lawful purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only part of a deposition is offered, adverse party may require introduction of all relevant parts; substitution of parties does not affect right to use prior depositions; depositions may be used similarly in later actions involving same subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories may be served on any party or entity representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may serve upon any other party written interrogatories to be answered in writing by the party served or, if the party is an entity, by any officer or agent who shall furnish information available to the party. Copies of interrogatories, answers, and related pleadings shall be filed and served on the presiding officer and all other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of interrogatories is not limited except by protective order; interrogatories may be served after depositions and vice versa unless ordered otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and timing of answers and objections to interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Each interrogatory shall be answered separately and fully in writing under oath or affirmation, unless objected to, in which event reasons for objection shall be stated in lieu of an answer. Answers signed by person making them, objections by attorney. Serve copies within 14 days or as allowed by presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answers may be used in same manner as depositions (§ 1.321(d)). Timely, complete, and sworn answers are required; objections must state reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to compel answers to interrogatories and definition of evasive answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may, within 7 days, move for an order with respect to any objection or other failure to answer an interrogatory. For purposes of this paragraph, an evasive or incomplete answer is a failure to answer; the motion must state the scope and detail of an answer that would be responsive and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responding party may file a response within 7 days and append an answer/amended answer. Additional pleadings should not be submitted and will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer's remedial powers for interrogatory noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If presiding officer determines an objection is not justified he shall order that the answer be served; may rule that right to object waived; may order amended answer and specify scope and detail and any procedural consequences (including adverse findings of fact and dismissal with prejudice) for failure to provide a full and responsive answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer can impose consequences to compel compliance; orders to compel answers are not subject to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and procedure for document production and inspection requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request any other party (except the Commission) to produce and permit inspection, copying, or photographing of designated documents, papers, books, accounts, letters, photographs, objects, or tangible things within the scope of § 1.311(b) and in possession, custody, or control, or permit entry upon designated land or property for inspection/measurement/surveying/photographing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of the request must be filed and served on the presiding officer and all parties. Production requests must describe designated items; scope limited to permitted examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to comply with or object to document production requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The party against whom the request was made must, within 10 days, comply with the request or object claiming privilege or raising other proper objections. If not complied with, the requesting party may file a motion to compel within five business days of the objection or claim of privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to compel must be accompanied by the original request and the responding party's objection or claim of privilege; presiding officer may order in camera inspection when resolving disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena issuance requirements and particularity for duces tecum
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for a subpoena ad testificandum shall be submitted in writing (unless on the record). Requests for a subpoena duces tecum shall be submitted in writing, subscribed and verified, and shall specify with particularity the books, papers, and documents desired and the facts expected to be proved thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoena requests must be supported by a showing of general relevance and materiality. Requests are submitted in triplicate and need not be served on parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena ad testificandum to enforce notice to take depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for issuance of a subpoena ad testificandum to enforce a notice to take depositions shall be submitted in writing; the request shall not be granted until the period for filing motions opposing the taking of depositions has expired or any motion has been acted on; the request need not be accompanied by a showing that relevant evidence will be adduced, merely that the person will be examined regarding nonprivileged relevant matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subpoena duces tecum may be requested contemporaneously to command production; but such requests are subject to § 1.313 and the duces tecum particularity requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena duces tecum to enforce production orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for issuance of a subpoena duces tecum to enforce an order for production under § 1.325 may be submitted with the motion requesting such an order; the request need only show that the documents/things contain nonprivileged matter relevant to the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer will apply the duces tecum particularity and relevance/materiality standards when granting subpoenas to enforce production orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to quash or limit a subpoena
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person against whom a subpoena is directed may file a motion to quash or limit the subpoena, setting forth the reasons why it should not be complied with or why it should be limited in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to quash challenge service, scope, privilege, burden, or other grounds; the presiding officer must give prompt notice and brief reasons for denial in whole or in part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of subpoenas: who and how
rubrics_metrics.description: A subpoena may be served by a U.S. marshal or deputy, Commission personnel, or any person who is not a party and at least 18 years old. Service is made by exhibiting the original subpoena, reading it to the person if unable to read, delivering the duplicate, and tendering fees for one day's attendance and mileage (unless issued on behalf of the U.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper form and tendering of fees (when required) are part of valid service; failure can be challenged by motion to quash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of service requirements for subpoenas
rubrics_metrics.description: If service is made by a person other than a U.S. marshal, such person shall make affidavit stating date, time, and manner of service. Reasons for failure to make service must be stated on the original subpoena by the person who attempted service. The original subpoena with return affidavit shall be returned forthwith to the Secretary or directed official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit proof of service or explanation of failure is required for proper docketing and enforcement of subpoenas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena forms and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpoena forms are available on FCC website as FCC Form 766 and are to be completed and submitted with any request for issuance. If granted, Original and Duplicate copies returned to requester and Triplicate retained by Commission; Original includes form for proof of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the official form ensures required fields are completed; Duplicate is given to witness and used for witness fee claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness fees and mileage for subpoenas
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses who are subpoenaed and respond are entitled to the same fees, including mileage, as are paid for like service in U.S. courts; fees shall be paid by the party at whose instance the testimony is taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tendering fees at service is required except when subpoena issued on behalf of the United States or its officers/agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance and enforcement of witness production nationwide
rubrics_metrics.description: The attendance of witnesses and production of documentary evidence may be required from any place in the United States at any designated place of hearing; in case of disobedience the Commission or any party may invoke the aid of any U.S. court to require attendance/testimony and production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoena enforcement may be pursued through federal courts when a witness fails to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule of evidence: exclude irrelevant, immaterial, unduly repetitious evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: In hearings subject to this subpart B, any oral or documentary evidence may be adduced, but the presiding officer shall exclude irrelevant, immaterial, or unduly repetitious evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer controls evidentiary relevance and may cut repetitive or immaterial matters to preserve a focused record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance and limitation of cumulative evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction of cumulative evidence shall be avoided, and the number of witnesses that may be heard on any issue may be limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer may limit duplicative testimony and restrict witness numbers to prevent unnecessary repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer may call for further evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: At any stage of a hearing, the presiding officer may call for further evidence upon any issue and may require such evidence to be submitted by any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should be prepared to provide additional evidence if requested to ensure full and fair resolution of issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of extracts from documents containing nonmaterial matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If material and relevant matter offered is embraced in a document containing other matter not material, the entire document will not be received; the offering party must present the original and true copies of the material and relevant matter taken therefrom in proper form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present extracts in duplicate with proper identification and allow other counsel to introduce other relevant portions if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English documents must be filed with authenticated English translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Every document, exhibit, or paper written in a language other than English which is filed must be filed in the original language together with an English translation duly verified under oath to be a true translation; each copy filed must be accompanied by a separate copy of the translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations must be verified under oath; file both original-language documents and translations for each copy submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits must be offered in duplicate and copies furnished to other counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: No document or exhibit shall be received or admitted in evidence unless offered in duplicate. When documentary exhibits are to be offered, copies shall be furnished to other counsel unless the presiding officer directs otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide duplicate originals and serve copies to opposing counsel; presiding officer can waive duplicate/copy requirement in limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical or physical reproductions of sound waves not admissible as originals
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless offered to prove or demonstrate sound effect, mechanical/physical reproductions of sound waves shall not be admitted; any party desiring to offer such matter shall have it typewritten on paper of prescribed size, identified, and offered in duplicate in same manner as other exhibits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To admit sound content, transcribe/type the asserted content and offer that transcript as the exhibit in duplicate per § 1.49.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tariff evidence may be received by reference with particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: If matter contained in a tariff schedule on file with the Commission is offered, the tariff schedule need not be produced or marked for identification, but the matter must be specified with particularity (tariff and page number) so it can be readily identified and may be received by reference subject to check with the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite tariff and page number precisely; the admission is conditional upon verification with the original tariff schedules on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of official records and certified copies
rubrics_metrics.description: An official record may be evidenced by official publication or by a copy attested by the officer having legal custody or by an appropriate certificate; foreign records have specified certification options by consular or diplomatic officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prescribed certification procedures and use seals or certificates from authorized officials depending on domestic vs. foreign custody of records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of lack of record via diligent-search statement and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Absence of an official record may be evidenced by a written statement signed by the officer who would have custody if it existed, stating that after diligent search no such record was found, accompanied by the certificate as provided in § 1.359.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this method to prove negative evidence (nonexistence) where appropriate; the statement and certificate are admissible as proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-testimony production-of-statement rule
rubrics_metrics.description: After a witness gives direct testimony and before excusal, any party may move for production of any statement of that witness in the possession of the party calling the witness, if reduced to writing and signed or otherwise approved or adopted by the witness; motion directed to presiding officer. If the party declines to furnish the statement, the witness's testimony pertaining to the requested statement shall be stricken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calling parties should be prepared to produce signed/adopted statements of their witnesses or risk striking the related testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed requirements for introducing statistical studies and other analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: All statistical studies (sample surveys, econometric analyses, experiments, etc.) must be described in a summary statement with supplementary appendices detailing assumptions, study plan, procedures, survey design (universe, sampling frame, sampling units), selection method, econometric model specification and reasons for assumptions, changes effects, alternative models record, experimental design and controls, observations methods and adjustments, formulas, standard errors, test statistics, computations, computer programs, and final results; summary descriptions of input data shall be submitted and actual input data made available upon request. Other studies must include study plan, assumptions, techniques, facts and judgments underlying conclusions, weights given to factors, alternatives considered, and input data lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive methodological transparency so that statistical analyses can be replicated and evaluated; be prepared to supply programs and raw input data upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony by speakerphone allowed only with consent and presiding officer approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If all parties consent and the presiding officer approves, testimony of a witness may be taken by speakerphone. Documents used by the witness must be made available to counsel in advance and other ground rules may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain consent of all parties and presiding officer approval; ensure documents are circulated beforehand and agree on procedures to preserve ability to cross-examine effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written hearing pleadings must conform and be specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Written hearings resolved on a written record must have pleadings submitted in conformity with specified sections (§§ 1.4, 1.44, 1.47, 1.48, 1.49, 1.50, 1.51(a), and 1.52); pleadings must be clear, concise, direct, pleaded fully with specificity, consist of numbered paragraphs, and be supported by relevant evidence. Assertions based on information and belief are prohibited unless in good faith and accompanied by declaration or affidavit explaining the basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal arguments must cite appropriate authorities and distinguish opposing authorities; supply copies of non-routine authorities; parties must maintain continuing accuracy of information and authorities submitted; attachments must be Bates-stamped or otherwise identifiable and cited by page; include contact information and certificate of service; each pleading must contain a written verification of good-faith basis and not being filed for improper purposes; defective pleadings may be struck; motions for waiver may be filed for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative case content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after completion of discovery, the party with the burden of proof must file an 'affirmative case' fully addressing each issue designated for hearing, including (1) a statement of relevant material facts supported by sworn statements based on personal knowledge, documentation, or other admissible materials and a full legal analysis, (2) citation to relevant Communications Act sections or Commission regulations/orders, and (3) the relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affirmative case must address all factual and legal questions in detail; assertions on information and belief are unacceptable unless accompanied by declaration explaining inability to ascertain facts; failure to address issues may result in adverse inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsive case obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other party may file a responsive case within 30 days of the affirmative case and must include (1) a statement of relevant material facts supported by sworn statements or documentation and a full legal analysis, (2) citation to relevant Act or regulations/orders, and (3) any relief sought. The responsive case shall respond specifically to all material allegations in the affirmative case and seek to narrow issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements of fact or law in an affirmative case are deemed admitted if not rebutted in the responsive case; be thorough and specific to avoid admissions by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply case scope and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who filed an affirmative case may file a reply case within 15 days of any responsive case. The reply shall contain statements of relevant facts supported by sworn statements and a legal analysis that responds only to factual allegations and legal arguments made in the responsive case; other allegations will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply is limited to addressing arguments raised in the responsive case; failing to file a reply is not an admission of allegations in the responsive case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other written submissions and presiding officer's discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may require or permit other written submissions such as briefs, proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law, or other supplementary documents, and may limit their scope or require additional information for full, fair, and expeditious resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to submit additional or limited-scope documents if directed; the presiding officer controls the scope of supplementary filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for oral hearing from written-record proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when a hearing is designated for a written record, a party may file a motion requesting an oral hearing after submission of all pleadings but no later than the scheduling order date. The motion must list genuine disputes as to outcome-determinative facts that cannot be resolved on the written record, list witnesses whose live testimony is required, and include supporting legal analysis and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer shall grant an oral hearing limited to testimony and cross-examination necessary to resolve the identified genuine disputes; the presiding officer may also, on their own motion after submissions, conduct an oral hearing if such disputes are found.
